page.layout: Two parallel columns on one printed page, left and right, separated by a vertical rule. Left column: lexicon entries (Hebrew forms with Latin glosses). Right column: lexicon entries, ending with a fragment "Kal," that runs on to the next page. No marginal notes, no footnotes, no catchword.

main_text.l: ære fecerunt eos, fut. Hiph. 3. f. & pl. m. aff. R. יָשֵׁב.
יָשַׁב, יָשַׁב, יָשַׁב, revertetur, יָשׁוּב reverstentur, fut. Kal, 3. f. m. & 3. pl. m. parag. Rad. שׁוּב.
יִשֹּׁב flabit; וַיִּשְׁבֹּ & perflavit, fut. Hiph. 3. f. m. Rad. נָשַׁב.
וַיִּשְׁבּוּ et collocabunt, praet. Piel, 3. pl. R. יָשַׁב.
יִשַּׁבְּחֶנָּה laudabit eam, & יִשַּׁבְּחוּנְךָ laudabunt te, fut. Piel, 3. f. & pl. m. aff. cum epent. Rad. שָׁבַח.
יִשְׂבִּיעֵנִי satiabit me, Job. 9. 18. pro יַשְׂבִּיעֵנִי, fut. Hiph. 3. f. m. aff. R. שָׂבַע.
יִשְׁבֵּנִי redire faciet me, יִשְׁבָּהּ eam, וַיַּשְׁבּוּ et facient redire, וַיַּשְׁבֵּהוּ et fecerunt redire eum, וַיַּשְׁבּוּם eos, fut. Hiph. 3. f. m. & 3. pl. m. aff. Rad. שׁוּב.
יִשָּׁבַע jurabit, יִשָּׁבְעוּ jurabunt, fut. Niph. 3. f. & pl. m. Rad. שָׁבַע.
וַיִּשְׁבַּע et adjuravit me, fut. Hiph. 3. f. m. aff. Rad. שָׁבַע.
יִשְׂבְּעוּ saturabunt, fut. Piel, 3. pl. m. R. שָׂבַע.
וַיִּשָּׁבְרוּ et fracti sunt, fut. Niph. 3. pl. m. à 3. f. m. יִשָּׁבֵר frangetur, Rad. שָׁבַר.
וַיִּשְׁבֹּת et quievit, fut. Kal, 3. sing. masc. Rad. שָׁבַת.
וַיִּשְׁבַּת et quiescere fecit, fut. Hiph. 3. f. m. Rad. שָׁבַת.
וַיִּשָּׂג et attigit, וַיִּשָּׂגוּ et attigerunt, fut. Hiph. 3. f. & pl. m. R. נָשַׂג.
יִשְׂנַב exaltabitur, fut. Pual, 3. f. m. R. שָׂנַב.
יִשְׁגּוּ errabunt, fut. Kal, 3. pl. m. à 3. f. m. יִשְׁגֶּה errabit, Rad. שָׁגָה.

page.notes: Hebrew forms were read from a small, heavily inked scan; the vowel points and consonants of most Hebrew words are doubtful and are not marked individually, so treat all Hebrew as needing a check against the original. The first Latin word "ære" (top left) is uncertain. The phrase "cum epent." in the left column has an odd mark before "epent." that could be a printing sign. The Latin "jutabit" in the right column is probably a misprint or blur of "jurabit" (the entry is for יִשָּׁבַע, "to swear"), kept here as the printer's likely reading. Right column ends with the fragment "Kal," which continues on the next page. Header marks ' above the running head are dots, not text.
